page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware utilizes an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. This configuration provides 4 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Local storage is bundled with 40 GB of SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core execution in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory performance represents a notable bottleneck, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the bottom 25%, although cached small-block read bandwidth remains average at 850.79 GB/sec.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU resources, this instance is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that benefit from high single-thread burst performance but do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core execution. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, text processing, software compilation, and basic database operations. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and SHA_NI supports cryptographic and vector-based tasks, though memory-intensive applications are constrained by the limited 8.0 GB memory capacity.
